findings.reason: the node's gate is red on arrival as written, so the measure must be narrowed to the two consolidated callers or crew_follow_commands.py added to the write scope.
findings.text: §16's done-when requires that "no other module calls os.open with O_EXCL to make a claim", but only two callers are consolidated and a third exclusive-create claim with its own bounded stale reclaim remains in reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:982 (the lift claim, docstring at :961 "any claim for the lift already exists", stale reclaim via LIFT_CLAIM_MAX_AGE_SECONDS at :988), a module outside §16's write paths

findings.reason: the deliverable's decomposition must drop the empty-claim grace from the shared responsibilities and leave it inside the caller-supplied staleness predicate, or the attempt caller's reclaim semantics silently change.
findings.text: §16 lists "the empty-claim grace" as part of the shared function while also stating the two staleness rules differ, but that grace is itself the dispatch path's staleness rule `_empty_claim_is_stale` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:420, keyed on _NODE_CLAIM_EMPTY_RECORD_STALE_SECONDS) and the attempt path has no equivalent — claim_next_attempt's grace is the pointer-and-LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS rule in `_claim_may_be_reclaimed` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:357) — so a shared function performing it would change claim_next_attempt's behaviour, contradicting the same deliverable's "Neither caller changes its behaviour"
